title: Present Simple + Adverbs of Frequency
grammarTitle: Present Simple — Review + Adverbs of Frequency
grammarNote: Present Simple описывает РЕГУЛЯРНЫЕ действия, факты, и привычки. На уровне A2 ты уже знаешь эту форму — сейчас добавляем наречия частотности (adverbs of frequency), которые точно указывают КАК ЧАСТО что-то происходит. Главное правило: наречие стоит ПЕРЕД основным глаголом, но ПОСЛЕ глагола to be.

grammarTable.subject: I / You / We / They
grammarTable.example: I study every evening. · They always review their notes.

grammarTable.subject: He / She / It
grammarTable.example: She usually wakes up at 7. · He often skips breakfast.

grammarTable.subject: I / You / We / They
grammarTable.example: I don't check my phone before coffee. · They never miss class.

grammarTable.subject: He / She / It
grammarTable.example: He doesn't eat breakfast. · She rarely goes to the gym alone.

grammarTable.subject: Do I / you / we / they?
grammarTable.example: Do you always sit in the front row? · How often do they meet?

grammarTable.subject: Does he / she / it?
grammarTable.example: Does she usually cook dinner? · How often does he review notes?

rows.example: I always wake up at 6:30. — no exceptions, every single day.
She usually has toast for breakfast. — most days but not always.
He often studies in the library. — more than half the time.
I sometimes skip lunch when I'm busy. — less than half, but not rare.
She rarely uses her phone during class. — almost never.
He never misses a lecture. — not a single time.

grammarExtra.title: Word Order — WHERE does the adverb go?

rows.example: I always review notes. · She never eats breakfast. · They sometimes play football.
He is always tired. · She is never late. · They are usually on time.
"How often do you exercise?" → "Three times a week." (not an adverb of frequency)
✗ "She goes always to the gym." → ✅ "She always goes to the gym."

grammarExtra.title: Spelling rules for He / She / It (+s)

rows.example: She has coffee every morning. · It is always cold in January.

rows.form: ✗ She go always to the gym.
rows.example: ✅ She always goes to the gym. — adverb before verb!
✅ He doesn't usually study. — 3rd person uses doesn't.
✅ Does she go to WKU? — after Does, use base verb.
✅ He never comes late. / He is never late. — not both together!

grammarTip:
Три правила, которые ты должен знать наизусть на A2:
① NEVER / ALWAYS / USUALLY / OFTEN / SOMETIMES / RARELY — перед основным глаголом: «She rarely eats breakfast.»
② После TO BE — после: «He is always busy.» — не «He always is busy!»
③ В вопросах и отрицаниях 3-го лица — ТОЛЬКО doesn't/does: «Does she always study?» — никакого -s у глагола после does!

💡 Запомни шкалу: always(100) → usually(80) → often(60) → sometimes(40) → rarely(10) → never(0)

exercises.text: She ___ reviews her notes the same evening.
exercises.hint: Adverb of frequency goes BEFORE the main verb: "She usually reviews..."

exercises.instruction: Write the correct form of the verb.
exercises.text: Amir ___ (go) to the library three times a week.
exercises.hint: Amir = He → goes (3rd person singular adds -s).

exercises.text: Choose the correct sentence about Zhibek.
exercises.hint: With "to be": subject + is/am/are + adverb. "She is always late." ✅

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct negative form.
exercises.text: Kamila ___ (not skip) class — she has a perfect attendance record.
exercises.hint: "never" = 0%. never + main verb (with -s for she): never skips.

exercises.text: ___  he usually eat breakfast before class?
exercises.hint: "he" = 3rd person singular → Does he usually eat...? (base verb after Does)

exercises.text: "He doesn't usually goes to the gym." is correct.
exercises.hint: After doesn't → base verb (no -s): "He doesn't usually go to the gym." ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose the adverb that means "approximately 80% of the time".
exercises.text: Which adverb fits a habit that happens most days, but not every single day?
exercises.hint: usually ≈ 80% — most of the time, but not always. "She usually studies in the evening."
study → studies. Consonant + y → drop y, add -ies. (carry→carries, try→tries)

exercises.text: How often ___ Zhibek go to the gym?
exercises.hint: Zhibek = she = 3rd person → Does she go...? Always use "does" for he/she/it questions.

exercises.text: Amir ___ (not use) social media in the morning.
exercises.hint: 3rd person singular negative: doesn't + base verb. Never 'don't uses' or 'doesn't uses'.

exercises.instruction: Where does "always" go in this sentence?
exercises.text: Kamila / is / late / always / for breakfast.
opts: Kamila always is late for breakfast.
Kamila is always late for breakfast.
Always Kamila is late for breakfast.
Kamila is late always for breakfast.
exercises.correct: Kamila is always late for breakfast.
exercises.hint: With TO BE: subject + is/am/are + adverb: "is ALWAYS late" ✅

exercises.text: "How often do you study?" is answered with a frequency adverb like "always" or "never".
exercises.hint: "How often?" is answered with expressions like "three times a week", "every day", "once a month" — not usually just "always".

questions.text: She ___ (go) to the library every Monday.
questions.hint: She = 3rd person singular → goes. Most verbs + -s.
3rd person negative: doesn't + base verb. 'have' stays as 'have', not 'has'.

questions.text: "___ she always study in the library?" Choose the correct form.
questions.hint: She = 3rd person → Does she always study...? (base verb after does)

questions.text: Which sentence has the correct word order?
questions.hint: With TO BE: subject + is + adverb: "He IS rarely late." ✅

questions.text: Which adverb fits: "She ___ eats breakfast — 0% of the time."
questions.hint: never = 0% of the time. "She never eats breakfast."

questions.text: The verb "watch" in 3rd person singular is: he ___.
questions.hint: Verbs ending in -ch → add -es: watch→watches, teach→teaches.

questions.text: "I ___ check social media before coffee." (= 0% of the time)
questions.hint: "I never check social media before coffee." = 0%, no exceptions.

questions.text: "She go always to the gym on Mondays." is correct.
questions.hint: ❌ Two mistakes: "go" → "goes" (3rd person); word order: "always goes" not "go always".

questions.text: Which is the correct negative sentence?
questions.hint: 3rd person negative: doesn't + base verb. Never 'don't' for she/he/it.

questions.text: Rank from most to least frequent: ___  (always / rarely / sometimes)
"How often ___ you go running?" — "___ a week."
questions.hint: "How often do you go running?" (I/you/we/they) → "Three times a week." — frequency expression, not adverb.
carry → carries. Consonant + y → drop y, add -ies. (study→studies, try→tries)

questions.text: Amir ___ his notes even when he is tired. (= no exceptions)
questions.hint: always = 100%, no exceptions. 3rd person: reviews (not review).

questions.text: "Does she goes to WKU?" is a correct question.
questions.hint: After Does → base verb (no -s): "Does she go to WKU?" ✅ Never "goes" after does.

opts: She is often tired after class.
questions.hint: Adverb goes BEFORE main verb, not between verb and adverb of place. "She often studies late." ✅

questions.text: Complete: "___ Kamila usually have breakfast?" — "No, she ___."
questions.hint: Question: Does + subject + base. Short negative answer: No, she doesn't.
